items_raw.text: What’s something your parents or grandparents did that you now realize was LEGIT genius parenting?

topComments.text: “You wouldn’t like it… It’s too spicy”.  Said about only the best/expensive foodstuffs, of course ;)

items_raw.text:
The scariest part of this list is how many of these don’t even sound ridiculous anymore.

A $25 fast food meal used to sound like something you’d joke about.

Now you can hit that number without trying very hard.

Same with daycare, housing, property taxes, insurance, and everything else that quietly eats away at a paycheck.

People love to say “just budget better,” and sure, bad spending habits absolutely matter.

But sometimes the math really did get worse.

That’s the part people shouldn’t pretend isn’t happening.

media.ocrText: May be an image of text that says 'Brennan Schlagbaum, CPA @Budgetdog_ Jokes that are going too far: -$25 fast food meals -Paying property taxes -$400k "starter homes" -3% raises with 4% inflation -Daycare costing more than rent -Working your whole life to "enjoy" 10 years of retirement Hilarious. Truly.'

topComments.text: The toughest financial conversations are the ones where both things are true. Managing money wisely matters, but so does acknowledging that many essentials have gotten dramatically more expensive. When housing, childcare, insurance, healthcare, and food consume a growing share of income, even disciplined people can feel like they're running harder just to stay in the same place.

items_raw.text:
Apparently buying the gas is the cheap part now.

That $13.06 supply charge almost looks reasonable until the rest of the bill shows up.

Then you get $96.12 for maintenance and infrastructure plus another $18.91 in public benefit charges.

Utility bills are starting to feel like airline tickets. The thing you actually wanted is only part of what you end up paying for.

topComments.text: $13 for gas and $115 for everything surrounding the gas.

items_raw.text:
A box of cereal is $7 now... and somehow there’s LESS cereal in the box.

I compared the SAME grocery order:

2020: $181.42
Today: $273.17

That’s $91.75 MORE.

A 50.6% increase for the same damn groceries.

Somehow we’re paying more while getting LESS.

Our paychecks sure as hell didn’t go up 50%.

PLEASE tell me I’m not the only one seeing this.

topComments.text: Must be California 🤣 cereal here is $4

items_raw.text:
Can’t overspend if you refuse to participate in society.

Honestly, this feels less like a budgeting strategy and more like self-defense.

Payday hits and suddenly Target, Amazon, DoorDash, and every restaurant within 10 miles start calling your name.

Sometimes staying home really is the cheapest hobby.
